stem: In 1054, Cardinal Humbert, the pope's envoy, laid a bull excommunicating Patriarch Michael Cerularius on the altar of which church?
options: the Church of the Holy Sepulchre
the basilica of St John Lateran
Hagia Sophia in Constantinople
the Church of the Holy Apostles
why: On 16 July 1054 Humbert and the other papal legates placed the bull of excommunication on the altar of Hagia Sophia, the patriarch's own cathedral in Constantinople; Cerularius answered with excommunications of his own.
source: Accounts of the events of 1054 (Humbert's bull; Cerularius's synod)

es.stem: En 1054, el cardenal Humberto, enviado del papa, puso una bula que excomulgaba al patriarca Miguel Cerulario sobre el altar de ¿qué iglesia?
options: la iglesia del Santo Sepulcro
la basílica de San Juan de Letrán
Santa Sofía de Constantinopla
la iglesia de los Santos Apóstoles
es.why: El 16 de julio de 1054, Humberto y los demás legados papales dejaron la bula de excomunión sobre el altar de Santa Sofía, la catedral del propio patriarca en Constantinopla; Cerulario respondió con sus propias excomuniones.

stem: Anselm of Canterbury described his theology as "faith seeking understanding" (fides quaerens intellectum). What does the phrase mean?
options: faith comes first, then seeks to grasp what it holds
reason must prove each doctrine before it is believed
understanding replaces faith once a person is learned
faith and reason study separate truths that never meet
why: In the Proslogion Anselm writes that he does not seek to understand in order to believe, but believes in order to understand: faith is the starting point, and reason works to understand what is already believed.

es.stem: Anselmo de Canterbury describió su teología como "la fe que busca entender" (fides quaerens intellectum). ¿Qué significa la frase?
options: la fe va primero y luego busca entender lo que cree
la razón debe probar cada doctrina antes de creerla
entender reemplaza a la fe cuando uno ya es instruido
la fe y la razón estudian verdades que nunca se tocan
es.why: En el Proslogion, Anselmo escribe que no busca entender para creer, sino que cree para entender: la fe es el punto de partida, y la razón trabaja para comprender lo que ya se cree.

stem: Gregory Palamas defended the hesychast monks of Mount Athos, who said that in prayer they could see God's uncreated light. With which New Testament event did they identify that light?
options: the star that led the Magi to Bethlehem
the Transfiguration on Mount Tabor
the tongues of fire at Pentecost
the light at Paul's conversion
why: The hesychasts and Palamas taught that the light the disciples saw when Jesus was transfigured on the mountain (by tradition Mount Tabor) is God's uncreated energy, and that the same light can be seen in prayer.
source: Gregory Palamas, Triads in Defense of the Holy Hesychasts; Matthew 17:1-8

es.stem: Gregorio Palamás defendió a los monjes hesicastas del monte Athos, que decían ver en la oración la luz increada de Dios. ¿Con qué hecho del Nuevo Testamento identificaban esa luz?
options: la estrella que guió a los magos a Belén
la Transfiguración en el monte Tabor
las lenguas de fuego en Pentecostés
la luz en la conversión de Pablo
es.why: Los hesicastas y Palamás enseñaban que la luz que vieron los discípulos cuando Jesús se transfiguró en el monte (según la tradición, el Tabor) es la energía increada de Dios, y que esa misma luz puede verse en la oración.

stem: A poor pilgrim arrives unannounced at a Benedictine monastery late in the day. According to chapter 53 of the Rule of Saint Benedict, how are the monks to receive him?
options: at the gate only, so the monks' silence is kept
only once he can pay for his food and lodging
after three days of fasting outside the walls
as Christ, with special care since he is poor
why: Rule of Benedict 53 says all guests are to be received as Christ, and that the greatest care is to be shown to the poor and to pilgrims, because in them Christ is received more especially.

es.stem: Un peregrino pobre llega sin aviso a un monasterio benedictino al final del día. Según el capítulo 53 de la Regla de san Benito, ¿cómo deben recibirlo los monjes?
options: solo en la puerta, para no romper el silencio
solo cuando pueda pagar su comida y alojamiento
después de tres días de ayuno fuera de los muros
como a Cristo, con más cuidado por ser pobre
es.why: La Regla de san Benito, capítulo 53, dice que todos los huéspedes deben ser recibidos como Cristo, y que se debe mostrar el mayor cuidado a los pobres y a los peregrinos, porque en ellos se recibe a Cristo de un modo especial.

stem: Martin Luther later wrote that his breakthrough came over "the righteousness of God" in Romans 1:17. How did he come to read that phrase?
options: as the justice by which God punishes the unrighteous
as the merit earned by keeping a religious rule
as the holiness reached through frequent confession
as the righteousness God gives freely through faith
why: In his 1545 preface Luther says he had hated the phrase, hearing it as God's punishing justice; he came to see it as the righteousness by which God makes sinners righteous as a gift, through faith, as in "the just shall live by faith."
source: Luther, Preface to the Latin Writings (1545); Romans 1:17

es.stem: Martín Lutero escribió después que su gran descubrimiento fue sobre "la justicia de Dios" en Romanos 1:17. ¿Cómo llegó a leer esa frase?
options: como la justicia con que Dios castiga a los injustos
como el mérito ganado al cumplir una regla religiosa
como la santidad alcanzada con la confesión frecuente
como la justicia que Dios da gratis por medio de la fe
es.why: En su prefacio de 1545, Lutero cuenta que había odiado la frase, porque la entendía como la justicia que castiga; llegó a verla como la justicia con la que Dios hace justo al pecador como un regalo, por medio de la fe, como en "el justo vivirá por la fe".

stem: In Zurich in 1525, Conrad Grebel, Felix Manz and their circle began baptizing one another as adults. Why, in their reading of the New Testament?
options: baptism must be given again after every grave sin
baptism should follow one's own confession of faith
baptism is valid only when done in a flowing river
baptism counts only when a worthy priest performs it
why: The early Anabaptists saw that in the New Testament people hear, believe and then are baptized, so they held that baptism belongs to those who can confess faith for themselves, and rejected infant baptism.
source: Early Swiss Anabaptists; Schleitheim Confession (1527), art. 1

es.stem: En Zúrich, en 1525, Conrad Grebel, Félix Manz y su círculo empezaron a bautizarse unos a otros siendo adultos. ¿Por qué, según su lectura del Nuevo Testamento?
options: el bautismo debe repetirse después de cada pecado grave
el bautismo debe seguir a la propia confesión de fe
el bautismo solo vale si se hace en un río que corre
el bautismo solo cuenta si lo da un sacerdote digno
es.why: Los primeros anabaptistas vieron que en el Nuevo Testamento la gente escucha, cree y luego se bautiza; por eso sostuvieron que el bautismo es para quienes pueden confesar la fe por sí mismos, y rechazaron el bautismo de niños.

stem: At the Diet of Worms in 1521, Martin Luther was told to recant his writings. What was his answer, and on what grounds did he say he could be moved?
why: Luther refused to recant unless he was convinced by the testimony of scripture or by clear reason, since popes and councils had erred; his conscience, he said, was captive to the word of God, and to go against conscience was neither safe nor right.
source: Luther's reply at the Diet of Worms, 18 April 1521

rubric.point: Says Luther refused to recant (would not take back his writings). Saying only that he asked for time to think does not count.
Names scripture and plain or clear reason as the only grounds that could change his mind. Naming only one of the two counts as partly.
Mentions his conscience being captive to the word of God, that popes and councils can err, or the later-remembered "here I stand" (optional, strengthens).

es.stem: En la Dieta de Worms, en 1521, se le pidió a Martín Lutero que se retractara de sus escritos. ¿Qué respondió, y por qué razones dijo que podía cambiar de opinión?
es.why: Lutero se negó a retractarse a menos que lo convencieran con el testimonio de la Escritura o con una razón clara, ya que papas y concilios se habían equivocado; dijo que su conciencia estaba cautiva de la palabra de Dios, y que ir contra la conciencia no era ni seguro ni correcto.

stem: In 1219, during the Fifth Crusade at Damietta in Egypt, Francis of Assisi crossed the lines to meet Sultan al-Kamil. According to the earliest witness, Jacques de Vitry, what happened?
why: Jacques de Vitry, a bishop in the crusader camp, wrote soon after that Francis preached to the sultan for some days, that the sultan listened closely, and that he sent Francis back safely to the camp with respect, asking him to pray for him. Later biographers such as Bonaventure add the offer of a trial by fire.
source: Jacques de Vitry, Letter VI (1220); Historia Occidentalis

rubric.point: Says Francis preached to the sultan (spoke to him about the Christian faith) and the sultan listened. Saying only that they 'met' counts as partly.
Says the sultan received him with courtesy and sent him back safely, unharmed, to the crusader camp. Saying Francis was martyred or imprisoned does not count.
Mentions the sultan asking Francis to pray for him, or that later accounts add the trial by fire (optional, strengthens).

es.stem: En 1219, durante la Quinta Cruzada en Damieta, Egipto, Francisco de Asís cruzó las líneas para encontrarse con el sultán al-Kamil. Según el testigo más antiguo, Jacques de Vitry, ¿qué pasó?
es.why: Jacques de Vitry, obispo en el campamento cruzado, escribió poco después que Francisco le predicó al sultán durante algunos días, que el sultán lo escuchó con atención y que lo mandó de vuelta al campamento sano y salvo, con respeto, pidiéndole que rezara por él. Biógrafos posteriores, como Buenaventura, añaden el ofrecimiento de la prueba del fuego.
